article.title: Postverbal arguments in Mandarin presentational clauses
article.part: Información y discurso avanzado — 信息與進階篇章
article.chapter: Sintaxis y discurso avanzados C1–C2 — 進階句法與篇章 C1–C2

claims.summary: Han analyzes the postverbal NP in Mandarin surface unaccusative structures as an internal argument originating in VP-complement position and remaining in situ.
Mei and Han present 人来了 and 来人了 as examples of Mandarin existential structures where the nominal argument may occur before or after the verb.
Han's minimalist analysis says a postverbal internal argument in a Mandarin unaccusative structure may serve as presentational focus or unmarked end focus.

Mei and Han propose a base-generated topic analysis for sentence-initial NPs, while Han's 2016 account analyzes postverbal NPs in unaccusative structures as internal arguments; the cited work does not establish one universally accepted analysis or Taiwan-specific frequency/productivity.

links.notes: The journal abstract explicitly identifies the postverbal NP as an internal argument in VP-complement position that remains in situ.

locator.section: 三、存现结构和非使役结构

links.notes: The article gives the contrasting examples 人来了/来人了 and 船沉了/沉了船, stating that the argument may occur before or after the verb in these Mandarin existential structures.
The abstract states that the retained postverbal internal NP serves as presentational focus or unmarked end focus.

locator.section: Abstract; 三、存现结构和非使役结构

links.notes: The authors propose base-generated topic analysis for sentence-initial NPs and discuss pre-/postverbal nominal patterns; this proposal is presented as their analysis, not a consensus result.
Han's later paper explicitly offers a distinct minimalist derivation for postverbal NPs in unaccusative structures.
